```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(ggplot2); library(DT) })
P   <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/GLI-Hedgehog_Signaling"
GS  <- file.path(P, "data/gene_sets")
r   <- read.delim(file.path(P, "results/1.geneset_enrichment/enrichment_fisher.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
cl  <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_clusters/maSigPro_clusters_hgnc.tsv"))
gs  <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "enrichment_gene_sets.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
bg  <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "background_protein_coding_hgnc.tsv"))
sf  <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "SFARI_cat1_cat2_07-12-2026release.tsv"))
ndd <- read.delim(file.path(GS, "NDD_genes.tsv"))

set_order <- c("TADA-high_fu2022", "TADA-med_fu2022", "TADA-high&med_fu2022", "NDD_wang2022",
               "SFARI_cat1", "SFARI_cat2", "SFARI_cat1&2")
r$gene_set <- factor(r$gene_set, set_order)
rc <- r[r$cluster != "all", ]                                  # 10 clusters x 7 gene sets
rc$cluster_f <- factor(rc$cluster, rev(as.character(1:10)))   # cluster 1 on top
pick <- function(k, s, v) r[r$cluster == k & r$gene_set == s, v]
f2  <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
pv  <- function(p) ifelse(p >= 0.001, sprintf("%.3f", p),      # p-value as text (ASCII)
                          formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1))
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

# chart ink and colours (diverging: blue = depleted, gray = no change, red = enriched)
INK <- "#0b0b0b"; INK2 <- "#52514e"; MUTED <- "#898781"; GRID <- "#e1e0d9"; AXIS <- "#c3c2b7"
SURF <- "#fcfcfb"; BLUE <- "#2a78d6"; RED <- "#e34948"; MID <- "#f0efec"; ORANGE <- "#eb6834"
th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.background = element_rect(fill = SURF, colour = NA),
        plot.title = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", size = 11),
        strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2), axis.title = element_text(colour = INK2),
        legend.title = element_text(colour = INK2), legend.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
        plot.caption = element_text(colour = MUTED, hjust = 0))
```

# Overview

## Question

GLI transcription factors mediate Hedgehog signaling, which shapes how neuronal
progenitors differentiate. In this experiment, GLI is overexpressed and then
perturbed or removed, and gene expression is measured over a time course. Genes
that respond were grouped into **10 clusters** by their expression pattern
(maSigPro).

**Hypothesis:** genes that respond to GLI perturbation are enriched for genes
implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.

| Analysis | Approach | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Autism | Enrichment with SFARI genes (category 1, 2, 1&2) | done |
| Autism | High- vs medium-confidence TADA genes (Fu et al. 2022) | done |
| Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) | Enrichment with Wang et al. 2022 NDD genes | done |
<!-- | Developmental disorders only | DD gene list | prepared, not run yet | -->
<!-- | Schizophrenia | MAGMA with GWAS summary statistics | planned | -->

## GLI-response clusters

All gene names were updated to current HGNC symbols. Only protein-coding genes
are kept, to match the background. Most dropped genes are lncRNAs, antisense
transcripts or pseudogenes.

```{r clusters}
k <- sort(unique(cl$cluster))
tab <- data.frame(cluster = k, genes_in_file = as.vector(table(cl$cluster)),
                  kept = as.vector(table(factor(cl$cluster[cl$kept], k))))
tab <- rbind(tab, data.frame(cluster = "total", genes_in_file = sum(tab$genes_in_file), kept = sum(tab$kept)))
knitr::kable(tab, col.names = c("Cluster", "Genes in file", "Protein-coding genes kept"),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Gene sets

```{r genesets}
def <- data.frame(
  set = set_order,
  source = c(rep("[Fu et al. 2022, *Nat Genet*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-022-01104-0)", 3),
             "[Wang et al. 2022, *PNAS*](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2203491119)",
             rep("[SFARI Gene](https://gene.sfari.org/), release 07-12-2026", 3)),
  definition = c("TADA autism FDR &le; 0.001", "TADA autism 0.001 < FDR &le; 0.05",
                 "union of the two (Fu's 185 autism genes)",
                 "615 NDD genes: de novo enrichment, FDR < 5% in at least one model",
                 "score 1 (high confidence)", "score 2 (strong candidate)", "union of the two"))
def$n <- as.vector(table(factor(gs$gene_set, set_order)))
knitr::kable(def, col.names = c("Gene set", "Source", "Definition", "Protein-coding genes"), escape = FALSE)
L <- lapply(setNames(set_order, set_order), function(s) gs$hgnc_id[gs$gene_set == s])
w <- ndd[ndd$source == "Wang2022", ]
```

* **SFARI Gene.** Curated autism genes, downloaded 11/17/2026 (Q2 2026 release:
  `r sum(sf$gene_score == 1)` category 1 and `r sum(sf$gene_score == 2)` category 2).
  Genes listed only as "syndromic" with no score, and category 3, are not
  included.
* **TADA (Fu et al. 2022).** The largest and most recent autism TADA analysis:
  63,237 individuals, combining de novo, inherited and case-control variants and
  CNVs. TADA gives every gene a false discovery rate, and the tiers use the
  paper's own thresholds.
* **NDD (Wang et al. 2022).** De novo variants in 46,612 parent–child trios
  (15,560 autism, 31,052 developmental delay). For each gene, the observed count
  of damaging de novo mutations is compared with the count expected from its
  mutation rate, using three models (chimpanzee–human divergence, denovolyzeR,
  DeNovoWEST). The paper also gives medium (`r sum(w$tier %in% c("high", "med"))`
  genes) and high (`r sum(w$tier == "high")`) confidence subsets; all 615 are
  used here. Two-thirds of the trios are developmental delay, so the list leans
  toward DD genes. It updates Coe et al. 2019.
* **The sets overlap.** `r sum(L[["TADA-high_fu2022"]] %in% L[["SFARI_cat1&2"]])`
  of the `r length(L[["TADA-high_fu2022"]])` TADA-high genes are SFARI category
  1 or 2, and `r length(intersect(L[["NDD_wang2022"]], L[["SFARI_cat1&2"]]))` NDD
  genes are SFARI genes. Results across gene sets are therefore not independent.

```{r overlap}
sets <- c("TADA-high_fu2022", "TADA-med_fu2022", "NDD_wang2022", "SFARI_cat1", "SFARI_cat2")
M <- outer(sets, sets, Vectorize(function(a, b) length(intersect(L[[a]], L[[b]]))))
dimnames(M) <- list(sets, sets)
knitr::kable(M, caption = "Shared genes between gene sets (diagonal = set size).")
```

## Test

**Fisher's exact test, two-sided**, for each cluster &times; gene set. The
2&times;2 table compares the cluster with the *rest* of the background:

|                  | in gene set | not in gene set |
|------------------|:-----------:|:---------------:|
| in cluster k     | a | b |
| rest of background | c | d |

**Background:** the whole genome, i.e. all `r fmt(nrow(bg))` HGNC
protein-coding genes. The question is whether cluster k is enriched relative to
the genome.

**Significance:** nominal two-sided p < 0.05, not corrected for the
`r nrow(rc)` tests (about `r f2(0.05 * nrow(rc))` would pass by chance). A
two-sided test flags depletion as well as enrichment, so results always show the
direction.

# Results

## Summary

```{r summary_numbers}
s <- rc[rc$p_value < 0.05, ]
v <- function(k, set) pick(k, set, c("overlap", "expected", "fold", "p_value"))
t6h <- v("6", "TADA-high_fu2022"); t6m <- v("6", "TADA-med_fu2022")
c2n <- v("2", "NDD_wang2022"); c2s <- v("2", "SFARI_cat1"); c2t <- v("2", "TADA-high&med_fu2022")
c1s <- v("1", "SFARI_cat2"); c10s <- v("10", "SFARI_cat1"); c5s <- v("5", "SFARI_cat1&2")
```

* **Cluster 6 is the main signal.** It is enriched for
  `r n6 <- sum(s$cluster == "6"); if (n6 == 7) "all 7" else paste(n6, "of the 7")`
  gene sets. TADA-high genes:
  `r t6h$overlap` observed vs `r f2(t6h$expected)` expected
  (`r f2(t6h$fold)`&times;, p = `r pv(t6h$p_value)`). Enrichment is stronger for
  TADA-high (`r f2(t6h$fold)`&times;) than TADA-med (`r f2(t6m$fold)`&times;),
  the pattern expected if the signal is real.
* **Cluster 2** is enriched for NDD (`r f2(c2n$fold)`&times;,
  p = `r pv(c2n$p_value)`) and SFARI category 1 genes (`r f2(c2s$fold)`&times;,
  p = `r pv(c2s$p_value)`), and weakly for TADA-high&med
  (`r f2(c2t$fold)`&times;, p = `r pv(c2t$p_value)`).
* **Cluster 1** is enriched for SFARI category 2 (`r f2(c1s$fold)`&times;,
  p = `r pv(c1s$p_value)`), and **cluster 10** weakly for SFARI category 1
  (`r f2(c10s$fold)`&times;, p = `r pv(c10s$p_value)`).
* **Cluster 5** is mildly depleted for SFARI genes
  (`r f2(c5s$fold)`&times;, p = `r pv(c5s$p_value)`).
* In total, `r nrow(s)` of `r nrow(rc)` tests have p < 0.05
  (`r sum(s$direction == "enriched")` enriched, `r sum(s$direction == "depleted")`
  depleted); about `r f2(0.05 * nrow(rc))` would be expected by chance.
<!-- * Pooling all clusters, GLI-responsive genes are enriched for every gene set -->
<!--   relative to the genome (fold `r f2(min(r$fold[r$cluster == "all"]))`–`r f2(max(r$fold[r$cluster == "all"]))`). -->
<!--   This may partly reflect that genes expressed in neural progenitors are -->
<!--   generally NDD-enriched, so genome-wide enrichment should be read with this in mind. -->

## Fold enrichment vs all protein-coding genes

```{r heatmap, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.8}
h <- rc
h$l2 <- pmax(pmin(log2(h$fold), 2), -2)        # fold 0 (no overlap) shows as the darkest blue
h$lab <- ifelse(h$p_value < 0.05, f2(h$fold), "")
h$lab_col <- ifelse(abs(h$l2) > 1.1, "#ffffff", INK)
h$alpha <- ifelse(h$p_value < 0.05, 1, 0.35)    # fade cells with p >= 0.05
ggplot(h, aes(gene_set, cluster_f, fill = l2)) +
  geom_tile(aes(alpha = alpha), colour = SURF, linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = lab_col), size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = BLUE, mid = MID, high = RED, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-2, 2),
                       breaks = log2(c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)), labels = c("<=0.25", "0.5", "1", "2", ">=4"),
                       name = "Fold\n(observed /\nexpected)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cluster",
       caption = paste0("Red = enriched, blue = depleted. Solid cells with numbers: p < 0.05 (nominal);\n",
                        "faded cells: p >= 0.05. Fold 0 (no overlap) shows as the darkest blue.")) +
  th + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), legend.key.height = unit(14, "pt"))
```

## Significance (−log10 p) vs all protein-coding genes

Two-sided Fisher p-values, signed by direction: positive (red) if the cluster
has more genes from the set than expected, negative (blue) if fewer. Numbers
are shown where p < 0.05 (−log10 p > 1.3).

```{r pheatmap, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.8}
pc <- rc
pc$slp <- sign(log(pc$odds_ratio + 1e-12)) * -log10(pc$p_value)   # signed -log10 p
pc$slp_c <- pmax(pmin(pc$slp, 10), -10)
pc$lab <- ifelse(pc$p_value < 0.05, f2(-log10(pc$p_value)), "")
pc$lab_col <- ifelse(abs(pc$slp_c) > 5.5, "#ffffff", INK)
cap <- pc[abs(pc$slp) > 10, ]
cap_txt <- if (nrow(cap)) paste0("; above the cap: ", paste0("cluster ", cap$cluster, " ", cap$gene_set, " = ",
                                 f2(abs(cap$slp)), collapse = ", ")) else ""
ggplot(pc, aes(gene_set, cluster_f, fill = slp_c)) +
  geom_tile(colour = SURF, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = lab_col), size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = BLUE, mid = MID, high = RED, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-10, 10),
                       breaks = c(-10, -5, 0, 5, 10), labels = c("<=-10", "-5", "0", "5", ">=10"),
                       name = "Signed\n-log10 p\n(+ enriched,\n- depleted)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cluster",
       caption = paste0("Numbers: -log10 p, shown where p < 0.05. Colour is capped at 10\n",
                        "(numbers are not capped", cap_txt, ").")) +
  th + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), legend.key.height = unit(14, "pt"))
```

## Full results table

All `r nrow(rc)` cluster &times; gene set tests (background: all protein-coding
genes; nominal two-sided p). Use the search boxes to filter.

```{r table}
tt <- rc[, c("cluster", "gene_set", "n_cluster", "n_set", "overlap", "expected",
             "fold", "odds_ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high", "direction", "p_value", "overlap_genes")]
for (v in c("fold", "odds_ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high")) tt[[v]] <- round(tt[[v]], 2)
tt$p_value <- signif(tt$p_value, 3)
datatable(tt, filter = "top", rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE,
                         columnDefs = list(list(targets = ncol(tt) - 1, width = "300px"))))
```
